reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about FeNiCrMn's mechanical parity with CoCrFeMnNi and the dominance of dislocation/recovery mechanisms, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) only discusses a different dual-phase AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy and provides general background on HEAs, offering no direct support for these key premises.
premises: Co-free FeNiCrMn retains comparable or better mechanical performance than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi
Dynamic properties of related HEAs are sensitive to loading regime and material condition
In as-cast FeNiCrMn, dislocation generation and dynamic recovery are the dominant rate-controlling processes
At high strain rates, limited recovery time promotes dislocation/twin accumulation, enhancing strength
At elevated temperatures, enhanced dislocation mobility allows recovery, reducing strength but increasing ductility
